topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional cancer treatment modalities alongside the systemic toxicities and efflux pump mechanisms that limit their efficacy.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies designed to exploit specific intrinsic vulnerabilities and checkpoint defects in cancer cells.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibition and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the mechanism of small-molecule kinase inhibitors against oncogenic drivers and the molecular mechanisms underlying treatment resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the design and therapeutic applications of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against tumor cell-surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell activation strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence for immune surveillance and examine clinical strategies to reactivate or engineer T cells against cancer.

topics.label: Overall progress, clinical challenges, and future perspectives in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize broad trends in cancer mortality, clinical trial complexities, and future therapeutic strategies across oncology.
